system.name: ReCycle
system.one_liner: a system for resilient DNN training that reroutes microbatches to data-parallel peers and adapts the pipeline schedule to tolerate worker failures without spare servers

content.subject: how Adaptive Pipelining reroutes worker W1_2's micro-batches to peer workers W0_2 and W2_2 when W1_2 fails

relations.what: the normal (fault-free) path is broken: W_1_2 has failed and cannot receive this output
W_1_1's micro-batches are rerouted to healthy peer W_0_2, which processes them alongside its own regular load
the remaining micro-batches from W_1_1 are rerouted to healthy peer W_2_2
the output computed on W_1_1's behalf is sent back to W_1_3, the original recipient of W_1_2's output
the other rerouted output is likewise sent to W_1_3
W_0_2 still forwards its own regular pipeline output to W_0_3 as usual
W_2_2 still forwards its own regular pipeline output to W_2_3 as usual

values.what: one concrete failure instance: worker W_1_2 (stage 2 of data-parallel pipeline 1) fails; its predecessor W_1_1's micro-batches are split across peers W_0_2 and W_2_2, whose extra output is sent to W_1_3
values.linked_by: colour (per-stage icon colour, per-pipeline arrow colour) and the W_x_y subscript notation, plus curved black arrows explicitly tracing the reroute
values.result_cells: not a computed table; the specific set of named workers involved in the reroute (W_1_1, W_0_2, W_2_2, W_1_3) is itself the worked example

content.key_idea: Because data-parallel peer workers at the same pipeline stage hold identical parameters, a failed worker's incoming micro-batches can be split across its healthy peers, which forward the extra output to the failed worker's original downstream successor.
content.reading_order: legend first (stage colours, pipeline colours, fault-free vs adapting arrow patterns), then the main grid left to right along each data-parallel row, following the two curved black arrows that fork around the red-X'd W_1_2 into W_0_2 and W_2_2 and back together into W_1_3

encoding.color_means: each pipeline stage (0-3) has its own icon-outline colour (orange/cyan/green/magenta), shared by the legend swatches; each data-parallel pipeline (0-2) has its own arrow/cylinder colour (blue/gray/gold); red marks a failed worker
encoding.line_style_means: solid arrows only; colour, not dash, distinguishes a pipeline row's normal arrows from the black curved reroute arrows; dashed lines are reserved for the grouping box and the legend divider
encoding.state_means: a failed worker is told apart by a red X badge over its (still stage-coloured) icon; its healthy peers are visually identical to any other active worker of the same stage
encoding.marker_means: no numbered markers; the red X is the only symbolic marker, and the small 'Fault-Free' vs 'Adapting to fault' legend pair explains what a curved black arrow around an X means before the reader reaches the main diagram
encoding.emphasis: the fork-then-merge shape of the two black curved arrows around the red-X'd W_1_2 visually isolates the one mechanism the figure exists to explain, against an otherwise uniform grid of same-coloured icons
reusable_patterns: a small 'before/after' legend pair (Fault-Free vs Adapting to fault) taught once, then reused unlabelled in the main diagram
a two-dimensional worker grid coloured on two independent axes (stage colour by column, pipeline colour by row-arrow) so a single failed cell's reroute stands out against both colour schemes
weaknesses: the paper text names the final recipient of the rerouted output as 'W_2_3' in one passage, which appears to be a typo for 'W_1_3' since the figure clearly draws both curved arrows converging on W_1_3, not W_2_3
the legend's 'Adapting to fault' mini-example uses generic unlabelled icons, so a reader must map it onto the specific W_1_2 case in the main diagram unaided

sections: §Adaptive Pipelines: Managing Failures and Rerouting Micro Batches
evidence: originally intended for \(W_1 2\), are dynamically re-routed to workers \(W_0 2\) and \(W_2 2\)
workers \(W_0\_2\), \(W_1\_2\), and \(W_2\_2\) are peers that hold identical parameters for stage 2
Adaptive Pipelining will redirect its input to workers \(W_0\_2\) and \(W_2\_2\)

summary: This figure gives one concrete worked example of ReCycle's Adaptive Pipelining: three data-parallel, 4-stage pipelines (12 workers W_x_y, coloured by stage 0-3 and by pipeline 0-2), in which worker W_1_2 has failed (red X). A legend first teaches the Fault-Free vs Adapting-to-fault arrow pattern before the main grid uses it: W_1_1's micro-batches, which would normally go straight to W_1_2, instead fork along two black curved arrows to W_1_2's healthy data-parallel peers, W_0_2 and W_2_2, which hold identical stage-2 parameters. Each peer processes the extra micro-batch alongside its own regular load, then forwards its own output onward as usual while sending the extra output back to W_1_3, the failed worker's original downstream successor. All other workers keep operating exactly as in the fault-free schedule.
summary_zh: 该图示ReCycle自适应流水线例子：3×4的12个worker中，W_1_2失效(红叉)；前驱W_1_1的微批次经黑色箭头分流给W_0_2和W_2_2，二者常规输出照发，额外输出汇入原下游W_1_3。
notes: worked_example corrected from the prior False to True: the specific named workers involved (W_1_2 failing, W_0_2/W_2_2 absorbing, W_1_3 receiving) are one concrete instance of the general mechanism and are themselves the content. layout.legend set to 'inside' as the closest available enum value; the legend actually sits to the left of the main diagram behind a dotted divider, which is not literally 'inside/below/right/per-panel'. layout.column set to 'double' as an estimate since the measured index left this field blank and the figure's rendered width (879pt) is far wider than this corpus's typical single-column figures.
